blocks.text: The Jellinek Society is a rehab centre dedicated to treating individuals struggling with addiction to alcohol and other substances. Named after Dr. E.M. Jellinek, a pioneer in the field of alcoholism research, the society’s approach is rooted in the belief that addiction is a disease that can be effectively treated through a combination of medical and psychological interventions. Dr. Jellinek’s influential 1946 study, The Disease Concept of Alcoholism, continues to inform the Jellinek Society’s approach to addiction treatment, which emphasizes the physiological phases of alcoholism.

blocks.text: The Jellinek Society’s recovery house is housed in the former home of esteemed women’s rights activist, Nellie McClung and her family. Best known as a suffragist, author, and legislator, McClung was also a prohibitionist who advocated for the strict regulation of alcohol consumption and trade. Her passion for social justice and concern for the negative effects of alcoholism on individuals and families perfectly aligns with the Jellinek Society’s commitment to supporting individuals in their journey towards sobriety and wellness. The historic nature of the recovery house lends itself to a uniquely supportive and inspiring environment that promotes healing and recovery.

centre.about_html:
Location in Edmonton

Jellinek Society is located in the Westmount neighborhood of Edmonton, Canada. This location is close to public transportation, making it easy to access the various resources in the city. The neighborhood is quiet and residential, providing a peaceful environment where men can focus on their recovery.

Community Engagement

Jellinek Society emphasizes community engagement as an important part of their recovery program. Residents are encouraged to participate in activities such as volunteer work, fitness classes, and hobbies. This helps men build a support network outside of the home and promotes a healthy, well-rounded lifestyle.

Outpatient Services

Jellinek Society offers outpatient services for individuals who have completed the residence program and want to continue their recovery journey. These services include ongoing counseling, peer support, and access to 12-Step meetings. Outpatient services also provide a way for Jellinek alumni to stay connected with the community and give back to those who are new to the program.

Jellinek Society- Center Overview

The Jellinek Society is a rehab centre dedicated to treating individuals struggling with addiction to alcohol and other substances. Named after Dr. E.M. Jellinek, a pioneer in the field of alcoholism research, the society’s approach is rooted in the belief that addiction is a disease that can be effectively treated through a combination of medical and psychological interventions. Dr. Jellinek’s influential 1946 study, The Disease Concept of Alcoholism, continues to inform the Jellinek Society’s approach to addiction treatment, which emphasizes the physiological phases of alcoholism.

The Jellinek Society’s recovery house is housed in the former home of esteemed women’s rights activist, Nellie McClung and her family. Best known as a suffragist, author, and legislator, McClung was also a prohibitionist who advocated for the strict regulation of alcohol consumption and trade. Her passion for social justice and concern for the negative effects of alcoholism on individuals and families perfectly aligns with the Jellinek Society’s commitment to supporting individuals in their journey towards sobriety and wellness. The historic nature of the recovery house lends itself to a uniquely supportive and inspiring environment that promotes healing and recovery.

Frequently Asked Questions About Jellinek Society

Who is eligible for the Jellinek Society program?

Men who are at least 18 years old, have completed at least 30 days of inpatient treatment, and actively engaged in a 12-step fellowship (AA, NA, or CA) are eligible. Candidates must also be either employed or actively seeking employment or educational training.

How much does the program cost?

The program cost is $850 per month in lieu of rent.

Does Jellinek Society offer outpatient services?

Yes, Jellinek Society offers outpatient services for alumni who have completed the residence program.

Where is Jellinek Society located?

Jellinek Society is located in the Westmount neighborhood of Edmonton, Canada.

Are family members allowed to visit?

Yes, family members are allowed to visit and participate in family therapy sessions.

What types of activities are available for residents?

Residents are encouraged to participate in volunteer work, fitness classes, and hobbies.

What kind of counseling is available?

Individual counseling and family therapy are available on-site.

Location in Edmonton

Jellinek Society is located in the Westmount neighborhood of Edmonton, Canada. This location is close to public transportation, making it easy to access the various resources in the city. The neighborhood is quiet and residential, providing a peaceful environment where men can focus on their recovery.

Community Engagement

Jellinek Society emphasizes community engagement as an important part of their recovery program. Residents are encouraged to participate in activities such as volunteer work, fitness classes, and hobbies. This helps men build a support network outside of the home and promotes a healthy, well-rounded lifestyle.

Outpatient Services

Jellinek Society offers outpatient services for individuals who have completed the residence program and want to continue their recovery journey. These services include ongoing counseling, peer support, and access to 12-Step meetings. Outpatient services also provide a way for Jellinek alumni to stay connected with the community and give back to those who are new to the program.

Jellinek Society- Center Overview

The Jellinek Society is a rehab centre dedicated to treating individuals struggling with addiction to alcohol and other substances. Named after Dr. E.M. Jellinek, a pioneer in the field of alcoholism research, the society’s approach is rooted in the belief that addiction is a disease that can be effectively treated through a combination of medical and psychological interventions. Dr. Jellinek’s influential 1946 study, The Disease Concept of Alcoholism, continues to inform the Jellinek Society’s approach to addiction treatment, which emphasizes the physiological phases of alcoholism.

The Jellinek Society’s recovery house is housed in the former home of esteemed women’s rights activist, Nellie McClung and her family. Best known as a suffragist, author, and legislator, McClung was also a prohibitionist who advocated for the strict regulation of alcohol consumption and trade. Her passion for social justice and concern for the negative effects of alcoholism on individuals and families perfectly aligns with the Jellinek Society’s commitment to supporting individuals in their journey towards sobriety and wellness. The historic nature of the recovery house lends itself to a uniquely supportive and inspiring environment that promotes healing and recovery.

Frequently Asked Questions About Jellinek Society

Who is eligible for the Jellinek Society program?

Men who are at least 18 years old, have completed at least 30 days of inpatient treatment, and actively engaged in a 12-step fellowship (AA, NA, or CA) are eligible. Candidates must also be either employed or actively seeking employment or educational training.

How much does the program cost?

The program cost is $850 per month in lieu of rent.

Does Jellinek Society offer outpatient services?

Yes, Jellinek Society offers outpatient services for alumni who have completed the residence program.

Where is Jellinek Society located?

Jellinek Society is located in the Westmount neighborhood of Edmonton, Canada.

Are family members allowed to visit?

Yes, family members are allowed to visit and participate in family therapy sessions.

What types of activities are available for residents?

Residents are encouraged to participate in volunteer work, fitness classes, and hobbies.

What kind of counseling is available?

Individual counseling and family therapy are available on-site.
